r3_note: Engine: فئة واحدة (16:49) = 'only one?'; زعلتكش عن (32:14) = her عن; إدام (51:19) = qdaam, plural of قديم. Medi's -at past endings (maratat 30:11, تلجات 36:45) are sound shape, not B5. The 40:24 أجو moment is one vocab row; the plural أجو/أجا was his own observation.

rows.why: Talking about his fiancée he used the masculine adjective; Amal recast it feminine with a question.
Same masculine adjective again after her 02:00 fix; she recast عيانة again and he repeated 'Yeah, عيانة' - its own slip per the brief.
rows.english: My fiancée is a bit sick.

rows.why: He put the verb before the thing that hurts; Amal recast with راسها before بيوجع (the brief's own example); 04:07 is a repeat.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He asked how to say cough; Amal supplied كحة - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: Men not. ... You're worried about. You're worried from.
rows.why: قلقان takes من; he used لـ and Amal said 'Men not' and explained 'worried from', he then said من نار.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another word for a fire starting - not given)
rows.why: He offered يبدأ for a fire starting; Amal said no, there is another word, and put it aside.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: He asked how to say taking care; Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
دير بال takes على; he went straight from بال to خطيبتي and Amal recast with على (she said it outright at 11:45).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.why: Missing على again after her 09:51 fix; Amal named it: 'بدير بالي takes على'.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: باليك is not a form; the 'your' ending on بال is بالك, which Amal gave (and noted it is the command).
After خلينا a bare present verb follows; he used past عملنا and Amal recast نعمل, he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: خلينا نعمل الدرس إنه، إنه تخطط-- تفتتلي.
rows.why: 'The lesson that you planned' needs اللي, not إنه; Amal only asked كيف يعني and moved on (my reading).
rows.english: Let's do the lesson that you planned.

rows.why: تفتتلي is not a word; he then said in English 'the lesson that you planned'. Amal only asked what he meant and gave no word, so it is let-pass. May also be an engine garble - low.
rows.r3_why: Real non-word for 'planned' (his own English at 15:13 confirms the meaning); Amal's كيف يعني shows she did not understand but supplied nothing. Separate piece from agreed A12 (اللي).

rows.medi_said: oh my gosh, what was sky? ... أنا نسيته.
rows.why: He forgot sky (tried عصافير as a question, she said that is birds) and Amal supplied سما.
Amal asked 'one?' to his غيم and he gave the plural غيوم (the engine wrote فئة واحدة for her 'one?').

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.right: بتطلع = rises / goes up (not بتتطلع = look at)
rows.why: He understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; she said No and explained بتطلع here = goes up; he then said 'بتطلع, not بتتطلع'.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same listening slip; the misheard word in her line is بتطلع, so that is the wrong piece.

rows.medi_said: does it has to do with Azan? ... أنا نسيت الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: أذان؟ No. أذان is the call to prayer. فجر.
rows.why: He said he forgot the word for dawn (أنا نسيت الكلمة) and guessed أذان; Amal supplied فجر. His سجر is a one-letter root slip of the word she then gave (S4), so the row is a didn't-know.
rows.r3_why: One moment, one row: a didn't-know (he said he forgot the word). D10 (سجر) is the same moment and a one-letter root slip.

rows.why: He added لو to غير for 'other than'; Amal said 'No لو. غير.'

rows.medi_said: الشمس و و يوم شو، شو في.
rows.right: غير شمس و يوم شو في
rows.why: She asked what is there OTHER than sun and day; he dropped غير and said الشمس with el-. Amal recast غير شمس و يوم, he asked 'غير الشمس?' and she repeated غير شمس (8eir + bare noun).
rows.english: what is there other than the sun and the day
rows.r3_why: Real voiced recast: he asked about the el- and she repeated غير شمس. A16 (8eir + noun).

rows.why: سما needs el- here (the sky), and it leads; Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated it.
Amal asked how to say dark at night; he said he forgot and she supplied عتمة.
'One' goes after the noun (شمس وحدة); Amal praised and only echoed واحدة.
rows.r3_challenge: Amal answered واحدة شمس with 'Mm-hmm. واحدة. Great job.' - she praised it and voiced no fix; his feminine واحدة was what she wanted. Word order (شمس وحدة) is only the reader's reading; may not be an error at all.

rows.why: After the noun تاني agrees: نجمة تانية; Amal echoed تاني and he fixed to تانية, she said مهم.
Fronted نجمة needs a pointer ending on the verb; Amal named the pointer rule and he said بشوفها.

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He asked if since is لسا, then لا; Amal said no to both and supplied من.
He said الأول (the first) for الهوا; Amal recast الهوا and, when he asked 'What I say?', told him he said الأول.
For 'different' he said بعيد (far); Amal asked 'What's the word?' and he ended on الهواء هون غير عن الهواء هناك at 32:47.
rows.r3_challenge: Amal accepted بعيد: after 'What's the word?' she only gave the preposition (عن) and said ممتاز to بعيد عن الهوا هناك (32:33-32:42). 'What's the word?' (32:08) may be asking for the preposition, not rejecting بعيد; غير عن (32:47) was his own later rewording. Possibly not a vocab slip.

rows.medi_said: بعيد من cuz it's comparative, right?
rows.why: He chose من; Amal gave عن (engine garbled the rest) and he asked 'always takes عن?' and used it.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time.
rows.why: aa5er + el- means 'the end of'; Amal explained and he switched to آخر مرة.
Subject مرة is feminine so كان must be كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he said feminine كانت.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين ... would be for the last three years. Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي for 'ago'; Amal said no, ago is قبل.
سنان is a different word (teeth - he said so himself); Amal asked 'What's سنان?' and gave سنين. A different lexical item = tier 1, not a wrong form of سنين.
rows.r3_why: Tier 1: سنان is its own word (teeth), not a form of سنة/سنين he invented.

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
rows.why: 'The wind came a lot' made no sense to Amal: she asked إيش يعني twice and gave 'it was very strong'; he then said الهوا كان قوي كتير. Her fix is about meaning (wrong verb), not the plural ending - he noticed 'it's singular' himself.
rows.english: the wind was very strong in the morning
rows.r3_why: Her voiced reaction is to the meaning (إيش يعني x2, then the English 'it was very strong'), so vocab tier 1. The plural أجو for singular الهوا was his own observation after her echo, not a fix she voiced. D12 is the same row.

rows.why: The object (the floor) must ride on the verb; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said نظفتها.
For things on the ground he gave a singular; Amal asked 'one?' (engine wrote وحدات) and he gave وردات.

rows.medi_said: Is it bee? Is it bee plants?
rows.why: He could not find 'plants'; Amal supplied زريعة.
He offered رمل for dirt/soil; Amal told him it means sand; he then found تراب and she said Great job, تراب is dirt or soil.
rows.r3_why: Wrong lexical item for 'dirt'; her 'رملة sand' tells him it is the wrong word (same treatment as agreed A21's guessed لا).

rows.medi_said: I don't, أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: He forgot 'stones'; Amal supplied حجر.
He meant the old streets (plural, قديمة); Amal recast الشوارع.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: 'Made with stone' used مع; Amal said just حجر ('are stone') and that 'made of' is different.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني; حجر تاني means another stone; Amal recast.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: مفضل is an adjective and takes no possessive ending ('Never takes pronoun ending', 54:56); 'my favorite' alone is المفضل عندي. Filed A7 like agreed A37 (same rule, same lesson).
rows.english: the second stone was my favorite
rows.r3_why: An existing bucket fits (A7 noun + adjective, as agreed A37 files the same rule), so not PROPOSE.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: Adjective goes after the noun; Amal said المفضل is an adjective and gave الحجر المفضل.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal: 'No ال first'.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: The adjective after الدرس needs el- to match; Amal said it is an adjective that follows ders and gave هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في as 'is' (his book 'isn't here'); Amal: 'في is not is. في is there is' - Arabic needs no word for 'is', just مش هون. That is C1, not a wrong vocab item.
rows.r3_why: Amal named the rule (في is not 'is'), which is C1 (no word for to be).
